title: Jubilant FoodWorks Ltd - 533155 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Jubilant FoodWorks Q4 FY26 call: management flags 100-120 bps energy-led margin hit and short-term pressure, with no quantified margin timeline; stores to rise to 230-250 in FY27.
summary.overview: Management said quarter-on-quarter like-for-like swings are noise and pointed to full-year LFL of about 7% over two years, against a 5-7% long-term target. Q4 LFL was about 0.2% per an analyst; the call did not restate a reported figure. The drop in average order value followed the cut in minimum order value from Rs 149 to Rs 99 to win share. Management reiterated the 200 bps margin improvement target over the long term but declined to say how long near-term inflation pressure would last. Energy (LPG/PNG) was quantified at 100-120 bps, which the company said it has passed on through pricing, while wage and labour-code costs were discussed as further headwinds.

segments.name: Dine-in
segments.commentary: Management called dine-in and takeaway the real challenge to solve; no dine-in figure was quantified on the call.

segments.name: Delivery
segments.commentary: Management said delivery continues to grow strongly and is the company's strength; delivery growth slowed from 28% to 10% YoY per the analyst's comparison. Delivery mix is 76%.

segments.name: New brands (Popeyes, Hong's, Dunkin')
segments.commentary: Management said the dilution from these businesses is ahead of plan and is being reduced by focusing on fewer areas.

guidance_outlook: Long-term like-for-like growth of 5-7% per annum; the 2-year figure has been about 7%.
Long-term 200 bps margin improvement target reiterated in shareholder letter; timing to reach it not quantified.
About 230-250 new restaurants planned for FY27.
Q1 FY27 LFL said to be better than Q4, with no figure given.
Management said it will avoid major price increases, which are 'out of the table' barring one or two quarters of pressure.
capex_capacity: About 230-250 restaurants planned for the year, with the model shifting to delivery-carryout stores of 600-700 sq ft in large metros.
Capex per store down ~20% YoY, nearly three years in a row, from kitchen resizing and remodelling.
Converting LPG ovens to electric and piped natural gas; company says electric is now comparable in cost as commercial LPG prices rose.
Electric fleet share is large, per management, which gives an advantage on fuel cost.
Some sites need more seating; company is adding seats where needed.
demand_pricing: Management said Domino's gained share in QSR and pizza per a Nielsen 50,000-customer panel and among 30-odd tracked players (delivery data only).
Minimum order value cut from Rs 149 to Rs 99 to match competitors; this lowered average ticket size.
Aggregators are growing faster than Domino's delivery, which management attributed to non-QSR and premium players.
Calibrated price increases taken; ~120 bps of pricing passed through against energy costs.
Management denied any rollback of April price increases, saying pricing changes are store- and discount-specific.

qa_highlights.question: Why did 2-year LFL CAGR decelerate from 9% to 6% QoQ, and delivery from 28% to 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said QoQ is noise and full-year LFL is about 7% over two years. Dine-in and takeaway are the real issue, and average order value fell after the Rs 99 minimum order cut.

qa_highlights.question: Can 5-7% growth and 200 bps margin expansion happen together?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is prioritised, that over 50% of costs are fixed, and that growth is the biggest margin driver. It remained optimistic on both.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 75.5% gross margin sustainable, and what is input inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited wastage reduction, premium launches, mix and calibrated pricing as structural. Energy is 100-120 bps, with wage and commodity inflation also rising. Management said it had no firm handle on total inflation.

qa_highlights.question: How long will margin pressure last?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it is difficult to predict and declined to give a timeline of one, two or three quarters; the company is recalibrating every couple of days.

qa_highlights.question: Is LPG exposure larger than peers, and can outlets move to electric?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said electric fleet and conversion help, that the LPG-electric cost gap has closed, and that business continuity risk is minimal.

qa_highlights.question: Did a system outage affect World Cup final-day sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said systems were not down; there was only a minor app downtime with quick recovery and no notable impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did realisations fall ~5% while gross margin rose 100 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not reconcile it on the call and referred the question to Investor Relations for an offline breakdown.

risks_watch: Near-term margin pressure from energy (LPG/PNG), wages (labour code, state minimum wages) and commodity inflation; the duration is not quantified.
Dine-in and takeaway weakness and lower average order value after the Rs 99 minimum order change.
Delivery growth slowing to 10% and aggregators outgrowing Domino's delivery.
Dilution from Popeyes, Hong's and Dunkin' continuing, though reportedly ahead of plan.
Reconciliation of ~5% realisation decline with 100 bps gross margin expansion, which was left for offline follow-up.
Q1 FY27 LFL and margin trajectory, given no numeric guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, share gains and store expansion, but cautious and non-committal on margin timing; management repeatedly declined to quantify how long inflation pressure would last. The tone was defensive when questioned on margin guidance and on the outage claim.
key_quotes: So therefore, I'm not too worried on the variation of 9% to 6%.
So from all accounts, right, store addition and expansion is not a worry, we would open similar to about 230 to 250 kind of restaurants this year.
But I think there is inflation. We're entering an inflationary environment; at least near-term inflation pressure is high.
But short-term pressure exist. Now will it be for a quarter, 2 quarters, 3 quarters, I think, at this stage, is anybody's guess, right?
